title: A Simple Dictionary
objective: Store and retrieve related values with a dictionary.

sourceAlignment.title: Python Crash Course, 3rd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Eric Matthes
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: A dictionary stores information as key-value pairs. Instead of finding a value by its position like in a list, you look it up by a key you choose — a name, an id, a label.
Dictionaries are written with curly braces. Each pair is written as key: value, separated by commas. You read a value back by putting the key in square brackets after the dictionary's name.
Keys are usually strings or numbers, and each key can only appear once in a dictionary. If you write the same key twice while building one, the second value wins.
explanation.rule: A dictionary maps each key to exactly one value — use the key to look the value up.
